distinct_grid_states:
TWO distinct 04:45 grids, plus the 05:15 successor that bounds them. They differ in ONE contract.

STATE A — 04:45 close, SiMSCI 5.10pm/5.40pm.
Nikkei 225 F 7.30am-2.25pm / 2.55pm-4.45am; FTSE China A50 F 9.00am-4.30pm / 5.00pm-4.45am; MSCI Singapore Free F 8.30am-5.10pm / 5.40pm-4.45am; MSCI Taiwan F 8.45am-1.45pm / 2.15pm-4.45am; MSCI Singapore Free NTR (USD) F 7.25am-6.30pm / 7.00pm-4.45am.
Witnessed by four SGX artifacts spanning roughly fourteen months: the 2018 (Apr) Trading Calendar (PDF authored 2018-04-11, served from 2018-05-21, live today), the chinaa50 product-page payload (capture 2019-01-16 14:47:25), the 2019 Trading Calendar (document date 2019-01-15, live today), and the products-list payload (capture 2019-02-04 20:09:05). Capture range as evidence: 2018-04-11 (document authorship) / 2018-05-21 (first SGX service) through 2019-02-04.

STATE B — 04:45 close, SiMSCI 5.20pm/5.50pm. Identical to State A in every other family; the SiMSCI T close moves 5:10pm→5:20pm and the T+1 open 5:40pm→5:50pm, close untouched.
Witnessed by one payload, captured twice: 2019-06-11 05:18:00 and the byte-identical revisit at 2019-06-21 08:04:19. Capture range: 2019-06-11 to 2019-06-21.

STATE C (bound only, out of remit) — 05:15 close, SiMSCI unchanged from State B. Capture 2020-01-09 05:12:11.

So the 04:45 state as a whole spans 2018-04-11/2018-05-21 through 2019-06-21 in SGX's own artifacts, and the 04:45→05:15 changeover falls in an unwitnessed window between 2019-06-21 08:04:19 and 2020-01-09 05:12:11. Nothing in this channel narrows it and no effective day is inferred.

Two cautions on the boundaries. First, State A's lower bound COLLIDES with the portal page: the 2018 (Apr) calendar prints 4.45am and Nikkei 7.30am from April 2018, while the portal capture of 2018-07-11 — three months later — prints 2.00am and 7.45am. Both are SGX-authored, they overlap in time, and they disagree; the 04:45 state therefore does not start cleanly after the 02:00 state, and any intersection served across mid-2018 has to face that conflict rather than assume a clean ordering. Second, the 2019 calendar prints "7.00pm to 4.45pm" (pm, not am) on three NTR (USD) rows — Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand. SGX's own product API prints "4:45 am" for those same three contracts four months later and the 2018 edition has no "4.45pm" at all, so it reads as a typo, but it is quoted as printed and not corrected.
